messages.subject: stat_smooth and predict
parts:
Please consider this small dataset, I am trying to predict
values for missing days represented with na's and add them
to the plot as red points. I can do this
by manually fitting the model and adding another column with the
predicted values but I wonder if there's a shorter more efficient
way.
I have a couple of questions:

1 - Are the predicted values the same as the ones generated by
stat_smooth()?
If so, Is there a way to see the values generated by stat_smooth()
instead of
using predict?

2 - I would like to either use gam or mgcv packages to smooth my
fitted values,
can any of these be used inside the stat_smooth call?

library(gam)
fishes <- structure(list(iddate = structure(c(1L, 12L, 14L, 15L, 16L,
17L,
18L, 19L, 20L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 13L), .Label
= c("1/1/2011",
"1/10/2011", "1/11/2011", "1/12/2011", "1/13/2011", "1/14/2011",
"1/15/2011", "1/16/2011", "1/17/2011", "1/18/2011", "1/19/2011",
"1/2/2011", "1/20/2011", "1/3/2011", "1/4/2011", "1/5/2011",
"1/6/2011", "1/7/2011", "1/8/2011", "1/9/2011"), class = "factor"),
passage = c(6L, 8L, 10L, 15L, 6L, NA, NA, 3L, 8L, 9L, 21L,
8L, NA, NA, 34L, NA, 33L, 2L, 6L, 9L)), .Names = c("iddate",
"passage"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -20L))
fishes

fishes$iddate <- as.Date(fishes$iddate, "%m/%d/%Y")
# add a column with the missed days as 'yes' and observed days as
'no'
fishes$estimated <- ifelse(is.na(fishes$passage),"yes","no")
# omit na's
#fishes2 <- na.omit(fishes)
fishes
str(fishes)
fish.mod <- gam::gam(passage ~ s(iddate),data=fishes,na.rm=F)
fitted(fish.mod)

# Can I attach the predicted to the fishes dataset instead of
creating a new dataset?
newd <-
data.frame(days=1:20,iddate=seq(as.Date("2011-1-1"),as.Date("2011-1-20"),by="day"))
predicted <- predict(fish.mod,newd)
predicted

# bind the two datasets
x <- cbind(fishes,predicted)

# extract the missed days and add them to the plot as estimated values
xx <- subset(x,estimated=="yes");xx
ggplot(x,aes(iddate,passage)) + geom_point() +
geom_point(aes(x=iddate,y=predicted),data=xx,colour='red',size=3) +
stat_smooth(size=2)

# Instead of using loess I want method="gam",formula=y ~ s(x) but it
doesn't work
ggplot(x,aes(iddate,passage)) + geom_point() +
geom_point(aes(x=iddate,y=predicted),data=xx,colour='red',size=3) +
stat_smooth(method="gam",formula = y ~ s(x),size=2)

# I get the following error and warnings
Error in pred$fit : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
In addition: Warning messages:
1: Removed 5 rows containing missing values (stat_smooth).
2: In newdata.predict.gam(object, newdata, type, dispersion,
se.fit, :
No standard errors (currently) for gam predictions with newdata

messages.subject: Re: stat_smooth and predict
parts:
Hi Felipe,

Try this in a clean session with only one of gam or mgcv loaded mostly
because there is enough confusion of environments with ggplot2 calling
functions internally without adding that extra layer of masked
functions. You also go to some unnecessary work to predict the
missing values. I eliminate this. Finally, I just use subset instead
of creating a special 'yes' 'no' column to indicate the missingness
that is already indicated by NAs in the 'passage' column. Oh, and I
put the red points after the smooth so they show up better.

fishes <- structure(list(iddate = structure(c(1L, 12L, 14L, 15L, 16L,
17L, 18L, 19L, 20L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 13L), .Label
= c("1/1/2011", "1/10/2011", "1/11/2011", "1/12/2011", "1/13/2011",
"1/14/2011", "1/15/2011", "1/16/2011", "1/17/2011", "1/18/2011", "1/19/2011",
"1/2/2011", "1/20/2011", "1/3/2011", "1/4/2011", "1/5/2011",
"1/6/2011", "1/7/2011", "1/8/2011", "1/9/2011"), class = "factor"),
passage = c(6L, 8L, 10L, 15L, 6L, NA, NA, 3L, 8L, 9L, 21L,
8L, NA, NA, 34L, NA, 33L, 2L, 6L, 9L)), .Names = c("iddate",
"passage"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -20L))

fishes$iddate <- as.Date(fishes$iddate, "%m/%d/%Y")

require(mgcv)
require(ggplot2)

m <- gam(passage ~ s(as.numeric(iddate)), data = fishes)
fishes$predicted <- predict(m, fishes)

ggplot(fishes, aes(x = iddate, y = passage)) +
geom_point() +
stat_smooth(method = gam, formula = y ~ s(x), size = 2) +
geom_point(aes(x = iddate, y = predicted),
data = subset(fishes, is.na(passage)), colour = "red", size = 3)

HTH,

Josh
